description: Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol attack surface (Linux Foundation v1.0, 2026). Covers agent card forgery, capability over-claim, recursive delegation abuse, missing caller allowlist, internal-URL exfil, tool description injection at the card layer. Distinct from MCP attacks (MCP is host↔server JSON-RPC; A2A is agent↔agent peering).

LLM prompt injection — direct (user-controlled prompt smuggling), indirect (via retrieved data), tool/function calling abuse, jailbreak chains, system-prompt extraction. Coverage spans GPT/Claude/Gemini/Llama backends and common wrappers (LangChain, LlamaIndex, Vercel AI SDK, OpenAI Assistants).

Anonymous cloud-service exposure expansion. Covers etcd, kubelet, Docker daemon, Consul, Vault, Nomad, Spinnaker UIs, Firebase RTDB/Firestore open-rules, Terraform .tfstate exposure, Lambda Function URL auth=NONE detection. Pure HTTP probes — no provider creds.

Argument injection — distinct from generic command injection. Application passes user input as an argument to a subprocess but doesn't validate flag-like prefixes. `-` / `--` / `@` smuggle behavior changes into commands the developer didn't intend (curl --upload-file, find -exec, openssl -config, ssh -oProxyCommand). PayloadsAllTheThings calls this out as its own surface; many CMDi-resistant apps fall to it.

Atlassian Confluence Data Center/Server edge CVEs — broken access control privesc (CVE-2023-22515) and OGNL template injection RCE (CVE-2023-22527). Detection-only version/endpoint fingerprints — NO state-changing OGNL.

Browser-side storage attacks — localStorage XSS persistence, ServiceWorker hijack, IndexedDB tampering, BFCache (back-forward cache) auth bypass, quota-exceeded fallback. These are CLIENT-SIDE bugs but reportable when chained or when the app trusts client-stored data.
GitHub Actions / GitLab CI injection + pwn-request patterns. Probed via poutine / octoscan binaries (run_poutine / run_octoscan), not HTTP matchers.
CI/CD pipeline and deployment configuration exposure — leaked env files, exposed build artifacts, misconfigured GitHub Actions, GitLab CI variables, source maps.
Citrix NetScaler / ADC / Gateway edge-appliance CVEs — path traversal (CVE-2019-19781) and Citrix Bleed memory disclosure (CVE-2023-4966). Detection-only fingerprints.
Clickjacking — missing X-Frame-Options / CSP frame-ancestors on state-changing pages. Promoted to active W11. Production MatcherEngine not_header schema (name singular).

Client-side request forgery — postMessage hijacking, window.opener (reverse tabnabbing) chaining, fetch from window.name, BroadcastChannel abuse, SharedWorker leak. These are FRONTEND attacks driven by an attacker page or stored content; chain with XSS/CSRF/open-redirect for impact.

Managed API-gateway misconfig detection: AWS API Gateway (REST + HTTP), GCP API Gateway, Azure APIM, Kong, KrakenD, Tyk. Common failure modes — stage-name leakage in URLs, AuthorizationType=NONE per-method, default 'test invoke' route exposed, IAM-protected mainline plus anonymous /Prod or /v0 sibling.

Direct-URL function endpoints: AWS Lambda Function URLs, Cloud Run, GCP Cloud Functions HTTP triggers, Azure Functions (auth_level=anonymous), OpenFaaS, Vercel/Netlify serverless functions. Often deployed with default IAM=NONE / no auth, leaving them publicly invocable. Operator-anonymous detection only — no provider creds.

Anonymous-access detection for cloud object storage across providers (AWS S3, GCS, Azure Blob, Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2, DigitalOcean Spaces, Oracle OCI, MinIO). Operator-anonymous (no provider creds). Covers HackTricks Cloud first-phase storage enumeration: list-bucket, public-read object, public-write authorization, ACL misconfig.

Cloud-native web app misconfigurations and SDK error matchers (AWS, GCP, Azure, Firebase). Detects leaked credentials, public buckets, exposed metadata services, SAS-token misuse, and cloud-SDK error fingerprints in HTTP responses.

Cookie tossing and SameSite bypass attacks — exploit browser cookie scoping rules to override, evict, or inject cookies from a sibling subdomain or via attacker-controlled responses. Chains with CSRF, session fixation, and cache poisoning.
CrushFTP edge-appliance CVEs — authentication bypass (CVE-2025-31161) and VFS/SSTI auth bypass (CVE-2024-4040). Detection-only endpoint fingerprints.
CSS prototype pollution / CSS custom-property injection — attacker-controlled CSS custom property (--var) leaks data via @import, attribute selectors, or background-image: url() exfiltration.

CSV/spreadsheet formula injection on export endpoints. Active in W12: csv_export_formula_reflection fires on responses with csv/spreadsheet Content-Type + literal formula prefix reflection. Existing contexts (formula_injection) remain as operator-driven payload guidance.
Default and common credentials for web admin panels, databases, and management interfaces.

Electron / Tauri / WebView2 desktop application security patterns. Mostly static-analysis-driven (binary inspection by desktop-agent); only autoupdate_http_mitm participates in auto_probe via HTTP. Reference contexts emit grep/probe instructions in their `detect` field for operator + desktop-agent.

DNS rebinding attacks — exploit time-of-check-to-time-of-use on DNS resolution to pivot from an attacker-controlled domain to internal/localhost services. Detects susceptibility markers: missing Host header validation, no DNS pinning, browser-resolvable internal endpoints.
DOM clobbering — HTML elements with id/name attributes overwrite global JS variables, causing same-origin attacks via stored content (comments, profile fields, markdown).
DOM clobbering 2024 — id/name → property collision + HTMLCollection clobbering

EchoLeak (CVE-2025-32711, Aim Labs) — zero-click indirect prompt injection family. Attacker plants instructions in document/email/image content that the LLM agent retrieves; LLM exfils private data via Markdown-image / link / hidden-HTML / CSS class channels. M365 Copilot was the named target; technique applies to any retrieval-augmented agent (Anthropic Claude, Cursor, GitHub Copilot Chat) that consumes untrusted content.
Cloudflare Worker / Vercel Edge / Fastly Compute internal-header trust + same-zone SSRF (2024-2025)
Edge Side Include injection — inject ESI tags processed by reverse-proxy cache layers (Varnish, Akamai, Squid, Fastly)

Cross-Site ETag Length Leak (PortSwigger Top 10 / 2025, #6 — Kaneko). The ETag header is a strong validator whose length / format encodes response size or content hash. When ETag is exposed to cross-origin requests (no-cors fetch, img/audio/video request), an attacker measures ETag bytes via cache or oracle to leak per-victim response size — yielding XS-leak of state (logged-in vs out, search-result count, message-count, account-balance bucket).
Microsoft Exchange OWA edge CVEs — ProxyLogon SSRF (CVE-2021-26855) and ProxyShell path confusion (CVE-2021-34473). Detection-only endpoint fingerprints.
Java Expression Language injection — JSP EL, JSF EL, Spring SpEL, OGNL in non-Struts contexts, MVEL, JBoss EL
F5 BIG-IP edge-appliance CVEs — TMUI RCE (CVE-2020-5902) and iControl REST auth bypass (CVE-2022-1388). Detection-only endpoint fingerprints.

GeoServer edge CVE — OGC filter evaluation RCE (CVE-2024-36401) via unsafe commons-jxpath expression evaluation. Detection-only: version/endpoint fingerprint + BENIGN arithmetic-echo marker (no command execution).

Engine-specific GraphQL attacks beyond the generic introspection/depth/batch covered by graphql.json. Hasura (x-hasura-admin-secret bypass, admin role escalation), Apollo (APQ poisoning, federation introspection), Dgraph (mutation auth), PostGraphile (RLS bypass via _ prefix), Strawberry (Python-specific). Auto-probe enabled — engine-fingerprint matchers gate execution.
HTTP/2 CONTINUATION-frame DoS (CVE-2024-27316) — endless CONTINUATION frames after HEADERS exhaust memory

HTTP/2 CONNECT internal port scan (PortSwigger Top 10 / 2025, #9 — flomb). HTTP/2 :method CONNECT with :authority targeting internal hosts/ports can establish raw tunnels through the front-end proxy. When the upstream allows arbitrary CONNECT, an attacker maps the internal network. Behaviour-based: TCP-open hosts respond differently from TCP-closed (timing or status), exposing the topology.

HTTP/3 (QUIC) attacks — 0-RTT replay, stream-reset poisoning, connection-migration auth bypass, downgrade to HTTP/2 or HTTP/1.1. Reference-only for now: requires HTTP/3 client tooling. Note: this file is in REFERENCE_ONLY in scan.py.
. v1.0 extension: 2025 desync variants — 0.CL, CL.0, V-H, Expect-100, RQP, double-desync.
Insecure randomness — UUIDv1 leak / short session ID / short reset token in URL. Promoted to active W12.

Ivanti Connect Secure / Policy Secure edge-appliance CVEs — auth bypass + command injection (CVE-2023-46805 / CVE-2024-21887) and stack-buffer-overflow RCE (CVE-2025-0282). Detection-only path fingerprints.

Kubernetes external attack-surface discovery (reference-only; auto_probe SKIPS this). Covers kubelet :10250 read-write API, kube-apiserver anonymous access, etcd :2379, Kubernetes Dashboard, ArgoCD, Tekton, Rancher, Portainer, container registries. Operator-anonymous — no kubeconfig / no service-account tokens required to surface these. Maps to HackTricks Cloud / Kubernetes section first-phase external recon.

Identify the LLM model and provider behind an API endpoint through behavioral probes. Detects model identity, tokenizer artifacts, refusal patterns, system prompt leakage, and provider-specific response headers/latency signatures.

Test LLM endpoints for tool-call manipulation, excessive agency, and function abuse. Covers OWASP LLM06 (Excessive Agency), LLM07 (Insecure Plugin Design), and tool-parameter injection via function-calling interfaces.

Apache Log4j 2 JNDI lookup RCE — Log4Shell (CVE-2021-44228). OOB detection ONLY: the payload carries the literal COLLABORATOR token which the runtime substitutes with a real Burp Collaborator subdomain; a collaborator interaction confirms the vulnerable log sink. Never hardcode a callback domain (Rule 9a).
MCP server attack surface — tool-description prompt injection, rug-pull, MCP-to-MCP confused deputy

MCP-38 threat taxonomy (arxiv 2025): tool-poisoning, parasitic tool-chaining, server-identity spoofing, capability lying, prompt injection via tool description. Applies to Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code Copilot Chat, any MCP-aware host. Use against MCP server HTTP/SSE/stdio entry-points OR against an LLM agent that consumes MCP tool listings.
MFA/2FA bypass techniques — step skip, code reuse, brute force, response manipulation

Mobile deep-link surface: Android intent:// URIs + intent-filter exported activities, iOS universal links (apple-app-site-association), iOS custom URL schemes, and Flutter / React Native router parameter injection. Reference-only — requires device + manifest inspection. Maps to OWASP Mobile Top 10 2024 M4 (Insufficient Input/Output Validation) + HackTricks Mobile section. Active in W8: deeplink_oauth_callback_backend_reflection + deeplink_webview_backend_loadurl fire on HTTP traffic captured AFTER operator triggers the deep link via am-start / mobile_adb_pack.
Progress MOVEit Transfer edge-appliance CVEs — SQL injection (CVE-2023-34362) and authentication bypass (CVE-2024-5806). Detection-only endpoint fingerprints.
Next.js cache poisoning chains (Allam 2025, PortSwigger). ISR (Incremental Static Regeneration) + RSC cache key manipulation + Server Action body confusion. Affects 13.x-15.x App Router.

. v1.0 chain-attack contexts: mix-up, audience confusion, JWKS swap, redirect_uri parser quirks (per draft-ietf-oauth-security-topics). 2026 H2: passkey step-up bypass (CVE-2026-32879) + WebAuthn API hijacking JS-injection.

OAuth 2.0 Device Authorization Grant (RFC 8628) — used by smart-TV, IoT, CLI tools. Phishing surface: attacker initiates device flow on victim's account, sends victim the user_code via social engineering (email, deep link), gets victim to approve at the verification URI.
DPoP token replay across resource servers — RFC 9449 + 2024 disclosures
Palo Alto PAN-OS GlobalProtect / management edge CVEs — GlobalProtect command injection (CVE-2024-3400) and management web auth bypass (CVE-2025-0108). Detection-only path fingerprints.

Parser Differentials (PortSwigger Top 10 / 2025, #10 — joernchen). Two HTTP / URL / header / body parsers in the same pipeline (front-end + back-end, WAF + app, framework + library) disagree on the same input. Attacker crafts inputs that one parser sees as benign and the next sees as exploitable — auth bypass, cache key confusion, ACL bypass, smuggling, internal-path access.

Payment flow abuse — Stripe / Square / PayPal / Adyen / Braintree integrations consistently yield $5k+ bounties. Common classes: payment_intent ID confusion, capture/refund races, webhook secret rotation, 3DS setup_intent reuse, idempotency-key per-customer scope, currency confusion, tax-zero exploits.

. v1.0 black-box variants: Express default-property pollution (json spaces / status), Fastify AJV pollution, Hapi event pollution, exec_argv RCE chain, side-channel sentinel detection. 2026 H2: axios PP gadget (CVE-2026-40175) for cloud-metadata exfil + proxy hijack; n8n core-node PP (CVE-2026-44789/90/91).

Push notification abuse — Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM), Apple Push Notification Service (APNs), web push (VAPID), and OneSignal. Common bugs: unauthenticated server-key send, push-token enumeration, silent-push exfil to mobile apps that handle silent payloads in background, cross-account token reuse on shared devices.
RAG context poisoning + direct vector-DB injection

React Server Components (RSC) Flight protocol attacks. Covers CVE-2025-55182 React2Shell (Wiz) and CVE-2025-66478 (Praetorian) — Next.js boundary-deserialization RCE via crafted x-rsc-form-state / Server Action bodies. Affects ~39% of cloud Next.js apps (App Router 13.x-15.x with Server Actions enabled). Markers: text/x-component, Next-Action header, $1@/$2@ RSC chunk syntax.

Response header injection beyond CRLF — injecting into existing response header values (Location, Content-Type, CSP, Link, X-Frame-Options) via user-controlled input that reaches those headers without newline sanitization. Chains with XSS (Content-Type text/html), cache poisoning (Cache-Control injection), and session fixation (Set-Cookie injection).

SCIM (System for Cross-domain Identity Management, RFC 7643/7644) provisioning endpoints. Used by Okta, Azure AD, JumpCloud, OneLogin, Workday, etc. SCIM endpoints are often LESS hardened than the customer-facing app: filter injection, mass user create with admin attrs, group escalation via PATCH, and tokenless POSTs are common 2024-2026 bug-bounty findings.
Service worker misuse — offline cache poisoning, scope hijack, push-subscription steal
Session fixation — attacker pre-sets a session token, victim authenticates with it, attacker hijacks the session

SmarterTools SmarterMail — CVE-2026-24423 unauthenticated remote code execution via the sysadmin connect-to-hub flow (SSRF-to-hostile-hub -> SystemMount.CommandMount blindly executed). Affects builds prior to 9511. Detection-only endpoint/product fingerprints; the hostile-hub weaponisation is operator-supervised (Rule 5 / manual_chain).

SOAPwn (.NET SOAP client + WSDL RCE — Bazydlo / watchTowr — PortSwigger Top 10 / 2025, #5). When a .NET application acts as a SOAP client and the WSDL endpoint is attacker-controlled (URL parameter, header, configuration), serving a hostile WSDL triggers .NET XmlSerializer code-gen + dynamic compilation. Reaching XSD imports and complex type definitions, attacker achieves arbitrary code execution in the SOAP-client context.
SonicWall SonicOS SSLVPN edge-appliance CVEs — SSLVPN authentication bypass / session hijack (CVE-2024-53704) and SSLVPN SQL injection (CVE-2021-20016). Detection-only endpoint fingerprints.
(core: error/union/generic/waf-bypass)
— blind variants (boolean / time / OOB exfil)
— engine-specific payloads (MySQL, PostgreSQL, MSSQL, Oracle, SQLite, NoSQL)
(core: cloud-metadata / internal / url-bypass / redirect)
— bypass variants (localhost / IPv6 / DNS rebinding)
— protocol smuggling + K8s in-cluster pivot
(core / language-generic)

Server-side template injection in Elixir template engines (EEx, Phoenix HEEx). New parent (2026-07): no existing SSTI parent covers Elixir. Error-oracle extraction per PortSwigger Top-10-2025 #1 (Successful Errors). Use against Phoenix apps rendering user input through EEx.
— Java engines (FreeMarker, Thymeleaf, Pebble)
— JavaScript engines (Handlebars, Nunjucks)
— PHP engines (Smarty, Twig)
— Python engines (Jinja2, Mako)
Multi-step state-machine desync — limit-overrun via timing-of-checks, two-window edges
JetBrains TeamCity edge CVEs — authentication bypass exposing REST admin (CVE-2024-27198) and auth-bypass RCE (CVE-2023-42793). Detection-only endpoint fingerprints.
Technology-specific vulnerability mapping. Used after tech stack detection to suggest targeted tests.

tRPC server-side prototype pollution via formDataToObject (CVE-2025-68130, GHSA-43p4-m455-4f4j). Affects @trpc/server experimental_nextAppDirCaller path on Next.js App Router. Attacker submits form fields named __proto__.X or constructor.prototype.X to pollute Object.prototype across the entire process.

Vector-DB / embedding-store attacks against RAG pipelines: Chroma, Pinecone, Weaviate, Qdrant, pgvector, Redis-vss, Milvus. Covers metadata-filter injection, namespace traversal, embedding extraction, anonymous-listing of indexes, RAG-poisoning via crafted upsert.
40x bypass surface — header / path / method / encoding / protocol tricks that flip 401/403 to 2xx on misconfigured ACLs, reverse proxies, WAFs, and admin route guards.

Web cache deception via static-suffix path confusion. Active in W13: static_suffix_cache_poisoning fires on cacheable response with user data word reflection. Existing path_confusion remains as operator-driven payload set.

WebAuthn / passkey bypass — most checks happen client-side or via untrusted attestation; recovery flows often weaker than the passkey itself. Bug-bounty payouts in 2024-2026 commonly exploit attestation-none acceptance, recovery-code reuse, PRF extension confusion, and fallback-to-password downgrades.

WebDAV (RFC 4918) misconfig: PROPFIND/MKCOL/COPY/MOVE/LOCK/PUT enabled on servers that don't need it. Beyond the PUT-method check in http_methods_enum — covers the full WebDAV verb set + auth bypass via PROPFIND on protected paths + LOCK-token DoS + COPY/MOVE to writable extension. Maps to OWASP WSTG 4.2.6.
Webhook abuse — replay of signed webhook events (Stripe, GitHub, Shopify, Twilio), signature bypass, timestamp tolerance attacks, idempotency-key reuse, downgrade from signed to unsigned variants.

Mobile WebView attacks: Android WebView (addJavascriptInterface RCE, file:// access, mixed-content), iOS WKWebView (postMessage handler abuse, file:// URL load), Cordova/Ionic bridge abuse, Capacitor plugins. Reference-only — requires device + ability to control WebView source URL or postMessage. Maps to OWASP Mobile Top 10 2024 M4 + HackTricks Mobile WebView section. Active in W10: 3 HTTP-observable contexts fire on backend traffic captured AFTER operator drives the WebView via am-start / mobile-dynamic-agent.

Microsoft Windows Admin Center (WAC) — post-authentication PowerShell command execution via the WinREST invokeCommand API (/api/WinREST/PowerShell/nodes/<node>/invokeCommand). The `script` property runs arbitrary PowerShell on the managed node as the WAC-connected identity. Detection-only fingerprints; command execution is operator-supervised (manual_chain). WAC gateway default port 6516; internal/HTB deployments commonly 6600/443.

XSS-Leak via Cross-Origin Redirects (PortSwigger Top 10 / 2025, #8 — Abello). Chrome's network connection-pool exhibits an observable oracle when a cross-origin request triggers a redirect to a same-origin URL. By exhausting the per-host TCP socket pool and timing pool reclaim, attacker infers the redirect target — leaking per-victim state (logged-in user, role, multi-tenant slug, OAuth flow position).

Archive-extraction path traversal (Snyk 2018 — Zip Slip). Triggers when application unpacks attacker-controlled zip/tar/7z/rar/jar without canonicalising entry names — `../../../etc/cron.d/x` lands outside intended directory. Reference-only: requires upload-then-trigger sequence + post-extraction filesystem observation; operator drives via file_upload tool. Maps to OWASP WSTG 4.10.8 + PayloadsAllTheThings 'Insecure File Upload'.
